newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures lost almost all of this week's gains as Bund weakness undermined an otherwise positive start which was helped by an opinion poll giving the French centre-right a majority in a May 25/June 1 election.

Traders said while there was no specific domestic news behind the French bond decline, many investors were lightening positions ahead of a three-day weekend and a U.S. monetary policy meeting next Tuesday.
Some said the contract would probably settle into a lower range next week although 129.40/50 should provide a solid area of support.
The June contract touched a high of 130.76 early on Friday, slipped back on a weak start by U.S. bonds and slightly stronger than expected U.S. data and then tumbled into the close with Bunds.
June PIBOR managed to hang onto some of its early gains, driven by non-resident buying on the back of an Ipsos poll giving the centre-right a seat majority, traders said.

Talk the Ipsos poll, released overnight, would show a swing to the opposition left had weighed on PIBOR late on Thursday, they said. At least two more opinion polls were due to be released on Saturday.
Analysts and traders said the market would probably be volatile next week on the back of poll rumours.

Most polling organisations will be conducting private polls but will not be making the results public as it is forbidden under French law to publish them in the week before an election or in the week between the two rounds of voting.

Although the opinion polls have continued to give the centre-right coaltion a majority in the National Assembly, analysts said the methodology used to calculate seats left room for large swings on the back of small shifts in voting intentions.
The French franc benefitted from the poll-related relief early on Friday, climbing as high as 3.3686 against the mark. It was at 3.3686 late in the session.
The Treasury managed to sell another 423 million francs of the five-year benchmark BTAN, taking the total value of BTANs sold this week to 21.51 billion, close to the 22 billion target.
The 10-year spread between French and German bonds was little changed at minus 14 basis points.
